title: Reset pager policy and burn-rate sensitivity after capacity regression
creator: Ava Chen
description: Follow-up from the 2026-02-16 capacity regression that produced multiple rapid SLO burn spikes and triggered noisy paging for tiered SLOs. This ticket consolidates action items to reduce alert noise while preserving fast detection for genuine capacity drops. Deliverables: updated paging rules, calibrated burn-rate windows per tier, canary rollout plan, and updated runbook guidance for oncall engineers.
postmortem_summary: On 2026-02-16 a capacity regression in the autoscaler caused transient latency and error spikes across a subset of serving clusters. Existing burn-rate alerts fired quickly and paged SREs repeatedly while the system recovered via existing fallbacks. Noise obscured root-cause signals and increased MTTR for unrelated incidents. We will adjust burn-rate sensitivity, introduce a two-stage paging workflow (pager for sustained critical burn, slack for transient elevated burn), and improve dashboards and runbook steps to reduce noise while keeping detection latency low.
investigation_notes: Initial incident: autoscaler regression increased queueing; 90th and 99th latency percentiles jumped for 12 minutes before autoscaler recovered (see dashboard link).
Burn-rate alert rules used a 3-minute window with a low tolerance for transient spikes; multiple alerts retriggered when background recovery retried pods.
Noise pattern: <50% of pages correlated with degradations that required manual intervention; remaining pages were informational while the system healed automatically.
Root cause: change in autoscaler cooldown introduced delayed scheduling during node churn (PR: github.com/redwood/autoscaler/pulls/1284).
Risk assessment: increasing burn window reduces pages but may delay human intervention for true regressions. We'll mitigate with a tiered policy and canary rollout.
action_items: Adjust burn-rate alert windows: increase critical tier from 3m->6m, adjust high tier to 10m with higher thresholds (owner: Diego Martinez).
Introduce two-stage notification: slack-ops channel for first elevated burn (info) and pager only after sustained critical window (owner: Priya Singh).
Add aggregation by customer tier and route low-impact customers to non-pager channels (owner: Platform Routing).
Create a canary rollout plan to deploy alert changes to eu-west-1 clusters first with 72h observation (owner: SRE oncall group).
Update runbook: explicit steps for verifying autoscaler health, when to escalate to pager, and checklist for follow-ups (owner: Liam O'Connor).
Create a Grafana dashboard panel that shows correlated autoscaler events, burn-rate, and paging history for post-incident analysis (owner: Observability team).
Ship a small client-side debounce in the alerting aggregator to suppress refiring within 2m unless severity increases (owner: Alerts infra).
acceptance_criteria: New alert config deployed to canary region and observed for 72h without missed critical regressions.
Pager volume for SLO burn alerts reduced by >=60% in non-actionable cases over a 7-day baseline window.
Runbook updated and reviewed by oncall rotation with acknowledgement from at least two engineers.
Dashboard shows clear mapping between autoscaler events and burn windows for 30 days of history.
